chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abdullah from Abu Ja'far, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, who said:
I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him): 'Regarding the man who is in need, is he liable for the Zakat al-Fitr?' He said, 'There is no Fitrah upon him.'

key_terms.الْمُحْتَاجِ: The needy person (one who lacks sufficient means)
key_terms.زَكَاةُ الْفِطْرَةِ: Zakat al-Fitr (the obligatory charity given at the end of Ramadan)
key_terms.فِطْرَةٌ: Fitrah (referring to the specific alms-tax of Fitr)

ai.seo_question: Is a poor person required to pay Zakat al-Fitr?
ai.summary: In this narration from Sahih al-Tusi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the financially needy (muhtaj) are exempt from Zakat al-Fitr, distinguishing this specific exemption from the general rules of Zakat. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that Fitrah is a purification for those who have surplus, thereby relieving the poor from the burden of giving when they themselves are in need. It reflects the broader Islamic ethic of easing financial obligations on the less fortunate during the festive occasion of Eid.
